papers.title: Consistent Distributed Invariant EKF SLAM with Point and Object Features
papers.abstract: Multi-robot SLAM allows robots to improve their estimates by exchanging map information, but repeated exchanges create unknown correlations between local estimators. Covariance intersection (CI) can fuse estimates without tracking these correlations. In right-invariant extended Kalman filter (RI-EKF) SLAM, however, point features obtain their invariant errors through the robot rotation, so a neighbor's map estimate is expressed in its own error coordinates and is correlated with its pose, and cannot be fused by CI directly. This paper presents Joint-CI, a unified fusion method for distributed RI-EKF SLAM with point, object, and mixed point--object maps. Using a neighboring robot's local posterior and an inter-robot observation, a joint estimate of the receiving robot's pose and the common features is constructed in the receiving robot's error coordinates, retaining the robot--feature and feature--feature correlations. Partial-state CI then fuses this estimate with the receiving robot's local posterior. We show that the unified formulation and the fusion preserve the six unobservable directions associated with global rotation and translation, and that communication and fusion preserve first-order covariance consistency given consistent local posteriors. Monte Carlo simulations and a real-world dataset-derived experiment show that Joint-CI improves estimation accuracy while maintaining consistent, mildly conservative uncertainty.

papers.title: SCOPE: Scene-graph Construction Optimized by Plan Error-correction for Robot Long-term Planning Datasets
papers.abstract: Task and Motion Planning (TAMP) stands as a fundamental challenge in robotics, essential for enabling autonomous agents to execute complex, long-horizon tasks in diverse environments. While Large Language Models (LLMs) introduce a new paradigm for TAMP by leveraging extensive common sense, their inherent reasoning limitations hinder direct application, and fine-tuning strategies to enhance these capabilities are currently bottlenecked by the scarcity of high-quality datasets. Existing automated generation methods often suffer from homogeneity, limiting model generalization, and unsolvability, where hallucinated scene graphs create physical mismatches with task goals. To address these issues, we propose Scene-graph Construction Optimized by Plan Error-correction (SCOPE), an automated framework designed to generate diverse and executable TAMP datasets. SCOPE incorporates multi-level diversity metrics to maximize the information entropy of scenarios. Crucially, it introduces a Plan Feedback Error-correction pipeline that utilizes planner execution failures as feedback signals to retroactively rectify logical inconsistencies in scene graphs, ensuring physical feasibility. Experimental results demonstrate that SCOPE exhibits greater robustness to erroneous scene graphs and generates higher-quality data. When utilized for LLM fine-tuning, SCOPE-generated data yield a downstream TAMP model that achieves an absolute 12.33% gain in success rate over its counterpart fine-tuned with data generated by DELTA, a state-of-the-art PDDL-based planner.

papers.title: Comparing local and global optimization reveals untapped hybrid potentials for machine learning-based inverse planning
papers.abstract: Machine learning (ML) models for normal tissue complication probability (NTCP) can be embedded directly into inverse treatment planning, but the resulting optimization problems are generally nonconvex, and the choice between global and local optimization involves a trade-off between optimality guarantees and computational cost. Two open-source frameworks for ML-based inverse planning were compared: OptiCL (global mixed-integer optimization via constraint learning) and pyanno4rt (local nonlinear optimization via end-to-end differentiation). Logistic regression, linear support vector machine, and feed-forward neural network NTCP models for grade 2+ xerostomia and grade 2+ radiation pneumonitis were embedded. Plan optimization was performed for eight head-and-neck (HN) photon cases and seven lung proton cases. The plans were compared by target coverage, OAR dose metrics, spatial dose agreement, post-hoc predicted NTCP, and runtime. A projection-based gradient approximation was introduced to embed decision trees. In addition to that, warm-starting, constraint strengthening, and pruning were investigated as hybrid strategies for combining local and global optimization. Comparing OptiCL and pyanno4rt across the HN and lung treatment plans revealed broadly consistent dose distributions. Mean differences (OptiCL}$-$pyanno4rt [95% CI]) were small: for HN cases, -0.16 Gy [-0.37, 0.06] (parotid) and -0.00 Gy [-0.01, 0.00] (PTV); for lung cases, -0.52 Gy [-1.10, 0.06] (total lung) and -0.04 Gy [-0.07, -0.01] (PTV). Mean NTCP differences amounted to -0.08 p.p. [-0.49, 0.33] (HN) and -1.73 p.p. [-2.68, -0.77] (lung). OptiCL tended toward lower OAR doses and predicted NTCP, but required higher wall-clock runtime. Hybridization of the decision tree-based HN plan eliminated 80% of binary decision variables without compromising plan quality.

papers.title: AI Enhanced Cerenkov Luminescence Microscopy
papers.abstract: Cerenkov Luminescence Microscopy (CLM) enables the visualization of radiotracer uptake in three-dimensional (3D) tumor spheroids but is limited by low photon statistics and spatial blurring caused by positron transport. Here, we present a Monte Carlo (MC)-guided deep learning framework for CLM image restoration. Using TOPAS/Geant4, we developed a physical model of heterogeneous 3D tumor spheroids to simulate positron transport, Cerenkov photon generation and optical propagation. A dataset of 15,360 paired degraded and idealized ground-truth (GT) images was generated from 80 simulated spheroid geometries and used to train a supervised Content-Aware Image Restoration (CARE) network. Compared with the self-supervised Noise2Void (N2V) denoising method, CARE achieved substantially lower reconstruction errors on synthetic validation data, reducing the mean squared error from 0.0492 to 0.0051. Training stability and noise robustness analyses further demonstrated high reproducibility of the restored images. The trained CARE model was subsequently applied to experimental CLM images acquired from 27 U87 tumor spheroids following 18F-FDG uptake. The restored images exhibited more localized intensity distributions and higher local contrast and signal-to-noise ratios compared with raw and N2V-processed images. These findings, aligned with the 3Rs principles of animal experimentation, demonstrate the potential of physics-based supervised restoration to mitigate both noise and positron-induced spatial broadening in CLM.

papers.title: Unified Projection-Domain Material Decomposition for Energy-Integrating and Photon-Counting CT
papers.abstract: Objective: To develop a unified and efficient method for projection-domain material decomposition in spectral computed tomography (CT) that incorporates an arbitrary number of spectral measurements, independent of the acquisition mechanism, without reducing the measurements to two effective energies. Approach: A nested optimization method was developed for two-material basis decomposition from K>=2 spectral measurements. It extends an existing two-measurement univariate method by replacing its polynomial approximation with profile minimization of the Poisson negative log-likelihood, reducing the inversion to two one-dimensional searches that use all measurements without spectral rebinning. The method was evaluated in simulation for energy-integrating (GE Revolution Apex Elite, Siemens SOMATOM Flash) and photon-counting (Siemens NAEOTOM Alpha) CT. Main results: The method recovered line integrals with noiseless iodine errors below 3e-6 g/cm^2 and noise within 3% of the Cramer-Rao lower bound (CRLB). Virtual monoenergetic images (VMIs) agreed, at 70 keV and above, with reference CT numbers and, on all three systems, with vendor VMIs of physical scans (mean absolute error 6-22 HU). For photon counting, four measurements instead of two reduced the iodine CRLB by 19% and image noise by 8-16% at every VMI energy, and lowered the regression error at 70 keV and above. Iteration and tolerance settings changed CT numbers by less than 0.04 HU, and decomposition took 0.34-0.67 s per million rays on an A100 GPU. Significance: The method provides fast, accurate decomposition for any spectral CT acquisition mechanism and number of measurements, so one method can serve every scanner in a virtual imaging trial.

papers.title: Quantitative Imaging of Scandium Isotopes with a Long Axial Field-of-View PET/CT
papers.abstract: Objective. $^{43}$Sc and $^{44}$Sc are positron-emitting isotopes of scandium that have attracted growing interest for theranostic applications in conjunction with the therapeutic isotope $^{47}$Sc. Both isotopes are non-pure positron emitters, and the associated prompt-gamma emission together with the high positron energy introduce complexities in achieving precise quantitative imaging. Approach. We evaluated the quantitative imaging performance of $^{44}$Sc and a $^{43/44}$Sc mixture on a long axial field-of-view (LAFOV) PET/CT using a NEMA IEC body phantom. We assessed contrast recovery coefficients, image noise and bias for different numbers of iterations and for absolute versus relative scatter correction, and implemented an isotope-specific point-spread-function (PSF) correction based on FLUKA-simulated positron ranges. Main results. The quantitative imaging performance of both isotopes is comparable to $^{18}$F, and the vendor's prompt-gamma correction effectively suppresses the additional random coincidences and lung error caused by prompt-gamma emission. The isotope-specific PSF correction further improves contrast recovery. While the bias obtained for $^{44}$Sc meets the EARL acceptance criterion for non-standard radionuclides, the bias for the $^{43/44}$Sc mixture exceeds it, which we attribute to the mixture-specific cross-calibration of the dose calibrators rather than to the PET imaging. Significance. Our results support the use of LAFOV PET/CT for quantitative imaging of scandium isotopes and provide practical reconstruction recommendations for clinical protocols.

papers.title: Direct Production of Ultra-High Radioisotopic Pure $^{64}$Cu from Natural Zinc Metal via D-D Fusion Narrowband Fast Neutron Source Irradiation
papers.abstract: Copper-64 radiopharmaceuticals have seen limited clinical deployment primarily due to the high cost of the isotopically enriched $^{64}$Ni metal required for its production. In this work we demonstrate that ultra-high radioisotopic pure $^{64}$Cu can be directly produced in a no-carrier-added-form from natural zinc metal through irradiation with D-D fusion narrowband fast neutron sources. A highly controlled D-D fusion narrowband fast neutron source at the ELI-ALPS Laser Facility was deployed to irradiate encapsulated 99.995\% pure natural zinc for 1 hour. Time-resolved gamma-ray spectroscopy of the irradiated sample over 72 hours was deployed to assess copper radioisotope activity. $^{64}$Cu was the only copper radioisotope detected within the irradiated sample, with a minimum and Minimum Detection Activity (MDA) threshold-corrected $^{64}$Cu radioisotopic purity of 99.62\% and 99.97\% respectively. Our result illustrates that highly controlled D-D fusion narrowband fast neutron sources have the potential to reduce the raw material production costs for $^{64}$Cu radiopharmaceuticals on the order of 2000 times. Cheaper $^{64}$Cu radiopharmaceuticals will increase their use in clinical practice, and, in-turn, increase outcomes for cancer patients receiving radionuclide therapy.

papers.title: Advancing oxygen-enhanced MRI acquisition and modelling through dynamic $ΔR_{1}$ and $ΔR_2^*$ sensing
papers.abstract: Purpose: To develop a multiparametric mapping framework for quantifying fat- and water-specific longitudinal and effective transverse relaxation rates, as well as changes in these parameters induced by a gas challenge. Theory and Methods: The proposed framework, termed SR-Fat DESPOT (single-reference fat-water separated driven equilibrium single-pulse observation of $T_1$), combines a two-component signal model with a single-reference variable flip angle (SR-VFA) approach. The signal model explicitly incorporates gas challenge-induced changes in relaxation rates. The single-reference acquisition strategy reduces data acquisition requirements while preserving sensitivity to both baseline parameters and dynamic changes. Sequence parameters were optimized using Cramer-Rao lower bound theory. SR-Fat DESPOT was evaluated using a modified open-surce abdominal numerical phantom and in two in vivo experiments: a single participant test-retest experiment and a pilot study with six participants. Results: In the abdominal numerical phantom, SR-Fat DESPOT was accurate for quantification of baseline relaxation rates with a normalized median absolute error (nMedAE) <3% for signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) >30 when comparing ground truth and estimates. SR-Fat DESPOT was also able to accurately recover median changes in relaxation rates, with differences within 0.001 $s^-1$ when compared to ground truth. In vivo, SR-Fat DESPOT measured changes in relaxation rates for spleen, kidneys, liver, and muscle under 100% O2 breathing, consistent with reports in literature. Changes detected in the spleen and kidneys were statistically significant across participants. Conclusion: SR-Fat DESPOT can quantify changes in relaxation rates induced by a gas challenge while reducing data requirements compared to more conventional approaches used in MR-oximetry literature.

papers.title: Reference Manual of MEDiml
papers.abstract: Radiomics is the high-throughput extraction of quantitative features (e.g., tumor shape, intensity distributions, and texture) from medical images to characterize tissues and uncover disease patterns invisible to the human eye. These features can serve as candidate imaging biomarkers for cancer diagnosis, prognosis, and classification. However, extracting thousands of features makes it difficult to identify the most informative ones for a given clinical task, while implementing an end-to-end workflow can require programming expertise that limits accessibility for clinical researchers. Hence, we propose MEDiml, an open-source, standards-compliant radiomics platform connecting feature extraction, predictive modeling, and interpretation through complementary graphical and programmatic interfaces. MEDiml combines a Python package (MEDiml-pkg) with a graphical desktop application (MEDiml-app) that enables researchers to conduct experiments without writing code. Both interfaces use the same computational implementation, and code generation exports graphically configured workflows as executable Python code, facilitating reproducibility and collaboration between clinical researchers and computational scientists. A typical MEDiml workflow includes image preprocessing, radiomic feature extraction, feature set reduction, model training and evaluation, and interpretation using feature importance. Feature sets can be grouped into levels of radiomic complexity (morphological, intensity-based, textural, and filter-based) to evaluate whether more complex features provide additional predictive value. This reference manual documents the radiomics concepts, workflow, software components, architecture, and installation, compares MEDiml with existing tools, and demonstrates its complexity-driven workflow on five oncological imaging cohorts comprising 2,104 patients. Resources: www.mediml.app.

papers.title: Toward opportunistic coronary artery calcium assessment from dual-layer dual-energy chest radiography using deep learning: a simulation study
papers.abstract: Background: Coronary artery calcium (CAC) predicts cardiovascular risk. Dual-energy (DE) chest radiography may enable accessible opportunistic CAC assessment by separating calcifications from overlapping bone. Purpose: To evaluate multi-task deep learning for CAC localization and CT-referenced score prediction and assess projection, image representation, and exposure effects. Methods: This retrospective simulation study used 550 calcium-scoring CT exams with reference CAC masks and Agatston scores. Dual-layer DE radiographs were simulated with a physics-based detector model. A modified nnU-Net jointly predicted CAC localization and scores from continuous probability maps. Comparisons included AP, 45°, and lateral views; lateral single-energy (SE), DE bone, and high-pass filtered DE bone images; and dose-matched models at 70, 50, and 24 mAs. Patient-level splitting reserved 10% for independent testing; five-fold models provided averaged inference. Metrics included Dice and AUC at CAC thresholds >0, >100, >400, and >1000, with bootstrap uncertainty and paired DeLong tests with Holm-Bonferroni correction. Results: Lateral views achieved Dice 0.34 versus 0.23 (AP) and 0.22 (45°), with AUCs for CAC >100 of 0.86, 0.81, and 0.77, respectively; AUC differences were not significant after correction. Lateral DE bone outperformed SE (Dice: 0.33 vs. 0.19; AUC for CAC >100: 0.86 vs. 0.64), with significant AUC advantages at >100, >400, and >1000. High-pass filtering added little classification benefit. Dice decreased with exposure, while AUC differences across doses were not significant. Conclusions: Simulation results support lateral dual-layer DE bone imaging for opportunistic CAC assessment, with significant advantages over SE. Physical and clinical validation is needed.

papers.title: Electric-field tunable spin texture in dual-gated HfS$_2$/graphene van der Waals heterostructures
papers.abstract: Spin-charge interconversion provides the essential link between spin information and electrical signals in spintronic devices. In spin-orbit coupled systems, spin-charge interconversion can contain multiple components associated with different spin-polarization directions, reflecting the underlying spin texture. Tuning this spin texture therefore provides a way to control not only the magnitude of spin-charge interconversion, but also the balance among its different components. Graphene-based van der Waals heterostructures provide an attractive platform for this purpose because interfacial spin-orbit coupling can host multiple spin-charge interconversion channels that couple to different spin-polarization directions. Here, we demonstrate electric-field control of spin texture in a dual-gated HfS$_2$/graphene van der Waals heterostructure, where independent control of carrier density and vertical electric field allows us to disentangle electrostatic doping from electric field-induced spin-orbit effects. Nonlocal spin precession measurements show that near zero vertical electric field, spin-charge interconversion is dominated by a spin Hall component with out-of-plane spins. Increasing the vertical electric field enhances additional in-plane spin components with Rashba-Edelstein-like character, including both parallel and perpendicular to the charge current contributions. These results provide experimental evidence that a vertical electric field can reconfigure the effective spin texture and control the corresponding spin-charge interconversion components, demonstrating electrical tunability of spin-orbit functionalities.

papers.title: The Spectroscopic Atlas of Excitonic Complexes in hBN-Encapsulated S-TMD Monolayers: From Excitons to Oxcitons and Beyond
papers.abstract: Hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) encapsulation has transformed the optical spectroscopy of semiconducting transition-metal dichalcogenide monolayers (MLs) by suppressing extrinsic disorder and enabling the resolution of an increasingly complex hierarchy of excitonic states. This Review provides a spectroscopy-oriented framework for understanding and identifying excitonic complexes in hBN-encapsulated Mo- and W-based MLs and their alloys. The discussion covers bright and dark excitons, Rydberg states, charged excitons, biexcitons, phonon-assisted replicas, and higher-order Fermi-sea many-body states, including hexcitons and oxcitons, with an emphasis on the experimental signatures that distinguish them. Particular attention is given to the combined use of photoluminescence and absorption-related spectroscopy, electrostatic gating, polarization analysis, excitation-power and temperature dependences, magnetic fields, and time-resolved measurements to establish microscopic assignments. The role of alloying as an additional degree of freedom for engineering the excitonic hierarchy, spin-valley configuration, and magneto-optical response is also highlighted. By organizing the rapidly expanding phenomenology around experimentally accessible fingerprints rather than individual material systems, this Review aims to provide a practical and broadly applicable guide for identifying, comparing, and engineering excitonic states in high-quality two-dimensional semiconductors.

papers.title: Quantum Interference Enhanced Rectification in Mesoscopic Nanowires
papers.abstract: Nanoscale nonreciprocal elements are needed to control signal flow in scalable quantum technologies, but existing nonreciprocal components are often bulky. Here, we show that a strongly nonreciprocal current-voltage relation can arise entirely from coherent elastic scattering in a mesoscopic Rashba nanowire with gate-defined scatterers. We first identify the symmetry constraints that enforce reciprocal transmission in a phase coherent conductor even when inversion and time-reversal symmetry are broken. We then show how gates that are capacitively coupled to the leads, together with a magnetic scatterer or transverse subband mixing, can remove these constraints. In the weak-scattering regime, nonreciprocal conductance originates from interference between distinct backscattering paths. In the strong-scattering regime, nonreciprocity can be resonantly enhanced by the hybridization of the transmitting channel with bound states that arise from a higher transverse subband or spin-split band. In this regime, we find that a bias-induced change in the gate potentials of about one percent can produce an order-unity diode response, i.e., electrons are transmitted almost as in a clean wire for one bias polarity, whereas for the other polarity the current is strongly suppressed.

papers.title: Interaction-Induced Bloch Geometry and Transverse Thermoelectric Transport
papers.abstract: Electron--electron interactions can reconstruct Bloch wave functions, changing their geometry and the associated thermoelectric response. We derive the linear thermoelectric response within the Hartree--Fock (HF) approximation using the thermal length-gauge density-matrix approach, resolving Drude, symmetric quantum-metric, and antisymmetric Berry-curvature contributions. In a noninteracting Bloch eigenbasis, we separate the reconstructed Berry connection into the noninteracting connection and an interaction connection. This gives bare, coherence, and interaction-connection contributions to the anomalous thermoelectric response. We determine the constraints imposed by spatial inversion, rotational, time-reversal, and combined symmetries on the three transport channels. In the relaxation-time approximation, the leading weak-broadening behavior is $Γ^{-1}$ for the Drude contribution, $Γ$ for the quantum-metric contribution, and $Γ^0$ for the Berry-curvature contribution. The interband scalings apply away from band degeneracies. Self-consistent calculations for the triangular-lattice extended Hubbard model illustrate how interactions generate Berry curvature and a quantum metric, change the symmetry of the system, and thereby contribute to transverse thermoelectric transport.

papers.title: Effect of Annealing on Maze Domains in Topological Insulator - Magnetic Multilayer Heterostructures
papers.abstract: Combining topological insulators with chiral magnetic multilayers offers the opportunity to greatly enhance the spin-orbit torque (SOT) driven manipulation of hosted spin textures, however this also exposes devices to the often poor temperature stability of the commonly used, Bi$_2$X$_3$-based (X is a chalcogenic element), topological insulator films. In this work we demonstrate through in-situ-annealing and polarised neutron reflectometry that the multilayer at a Bi$_2$Se$_3$ interface remains magnetically robust up to a temperature of 350 $^{\circ}$C: even as the Bi$_2$Se$_3$ epilayer structurally deteriorates. Through x-ray photoemission electron microscopy, an intermediate annealing temperature of $\sim$ 200 $^{\circ}$C was found to improve the domain ordering of the multilayer, allowing for field-induced skyrmion nucleation, all whilst sustaining minimal damage to the topological insulator

papers.title: Higher-order Angular Momentum Transport of Alteraxial Phonons in 2D Magnets
papers.abstract: The coupling between lattice vibrations and magnetic order in two-dimensional (2D) magnets gives rise to a variety of physical phenomena, among which magnetic effects of axial phonons carrying phonon angular momentum (PAM) have attracted considerable interest. However, a systematic classification of axial phonons in 2D magnets that covers their multipolar patterns and the resulting transport manifestations remains largely unexplored. Here, based on symmetry analysis, we classify all 2D magnetic point groups by their long-wavelength PAM wave patterns. Beyond the s-wave axial phonon, we identify alteraxial phonons with p-, d-, f-, g-, and i-wave multipolar textures, characterized by 1, 2, 3, 4, and 6 zero-PAM nodal lines, respectively. We then develop a theory of nonlinear PAM transport driven by a temperature gradient and derive two selection rules: a parity selection rule that determines whether the response occurs at even or odd orders, and an angular-harmonic selection rule that fixes the lowest allowed order for each wave pattern. The multipolar PAM patterns and selection rules are exemplified by two effective lattice models realizing f-wave and d-wave PAM patterns, respectivley. The angular dependence of the nonlinear PAM current reflects the underlying multipolar PAM texture, offering a signature for experiments. Our results establish a symmetry-guided framework for detecting and utilizing higher-order PAM textures in 2D magnets.

papers.title: Orientation-selective microwave heating of laser-graphitized diamond at 2.45 GHz
papers.abstract: Pristine diamond couples negligibly to a 2.45 GHz field. We show that femtosecond-laser inscription of a buried graphitic (sp2) architecture makes a 4 x 4 x 2 mm^3 N-doped (100 ppm) high-pressure high- temperature (HPHT) crystal absorb strongly, and that the absorption is switched by the orientation of the inscribed structure relative to the cavity electric field. With the 1.8 mm depth of a concentric grating along E, stepped power gave a smooth staircase to an indicated ~500C at 80 W followed, at 90 W, by an abrupt excursion to an indicated ~900C with surface roughening and terraced oxidation. Rotating the same sample so that the grating diameter lay along E, and an unmodified crystal in either orientation, gave no signal above the ~40C floor. We account for this by the depolarisation factors L of the sub-wavelength tracks, collapsed into one screening parameter S = Lσ/(ωε0εh), here, σ conductivity, ω - cyclic frequency, εh,0 - permittivity of host and vacuum, respectively. The model turns element length, diameter and writing regime into design variables for microwave absorption in a transparent host.

papers.title: Ferroelastic Reversal Magnon Thermal Hall Effect in a Fully Compensated Ferrimagnet
papers.abstract: Magnons offer a charge-neutral channel for spin and heat transport, yet reversible and nonvolatile control of their thermal Hall response poses a fundamental challenge in systems with zero net magnetization. Here, we establish ferroelastic switching as an effective route to manipulate magnonic transverse responses in fully compensated ferrimagnets. A minimal Heisenberg-Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya model reveals that ferroelastic switching can re-orientate the lattice anisotropy, which reconstructs the chirality-resolved magnon bands and Berry curvature distribution. Consequently, the two orthogonal fully compensated ferrimagnetic variants related by [C2||C4z] exhibit magnon thermal Hall responses with opposite signs, whereas the response vanishes in the intermediate altermagnetic phase. First-principles calculations further identify monolayer V2SSe as a promising material candidate for realizing the proposed ferroelastic control of transverse magnon transport. Remarkably, ferroelastic switching drives a dual magnonic-electronic band reconstruction, enabling nonvolatile reversal of the magnon thermal Hall effect while producing anisotropic orbital Hall responses and distinct magneto-optical spectra as complementary transport and optical fingerprints. Our findings establish ferroelasticity as an effective route to nonvolatile magnon control and multichannel state identification in zero net magnetization systems.

papers.title: Reinforcement learning for hardware acceleration and system-level optimization on FPGA and integrated-circuit platforms: A survey
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) enables adaptive and autonomous decision-making in embedded, edge, and heterogeneous computing systems. Field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs) and integrated circuits (ICs) offer low latency, energy efficiency, and architectural flexibility for RL deployment, while introducing challenges in resource constraints, implementation complexity, and hardware-algorithm co-design. This review surveys more than 100 studies on RL implementations across FPGA and IC platforms, emphasizing architectures, implementation strategies, performance evaluation, and applications. The literature is organized by RL family, including model-based Markov decision processes, classical value-based methods, deep RL, actor-critic, policy-gradient, and multi-agent approaches. We further classify studies by abstraction level, hardware realization strategy, and application domain, examining how RL algorithms map onto reconfigurable and fixed hardware. Unlike surveys restricted to particular algorithms or platforms, this work provides a unified analysis of FPGA and IC implementations, covering acceleration, reconfigurable architectures, energy-aware control, and system-level optimization. Comparative assessments consider resource utilization, latency, throughput, power consumption, and reported performance gains. Finally, we identify recurring architectural patterns, practical limitations, open challenges, and research directions for efficient RL-driven hardware systems. The survey offers a consolidated reference for researchers developing and evaluating RL solutions on specialized hardware.

papers.title: Hard and Soft Real-Time DNN Inference Scheduling on Heterogeneous Multi-Accelerator Systems via Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: We present a scheduling framework for heterogeneous multi-accelerator systems executing both hard real-time and soft real-time QoS-aware DNN inference workloads. The framework combines an online reinforcement learning (RL) scheduler with a deterministic runtime safety layer. The RL scheduler dynamically generates candidate schedules by jointly selecting sub-job priorities and accelerator assignments, while runtime certification guarantees that all HRT deadlines remain satisfied independently of the learned policy. To enable runtime certification in heterogeneous precedence-constrained systems, we introduce a schedulability-preserving prefix replacement criterion based on machine-wise cuts. The proposed criterion guarantees that runtime-generated schedule prefixes preserve the existence of a feasible continuation without requiring complete finish-time dominance with respect to a feasible reference schedule. Experimental results on heterogeneous DNN accelerator platforms show that the proposed framework preserves HRT schedulability while improving QoS-aware deadline satisfaction, client-level service quality, and accelerator utilization compared to state-of-the-art scheduling approaches.

papers.title: SnakeCharmer: Orchestrating Utility, Timeliness, and Placement in GPU Prefetching
papers.abstract: GPUs rely on massive thread-level parallelism to tolerate long memory latency, yet they still suffer severe stalls when many warps simultaneously wait for data from the memory system. Address-prediction-based GPU prefetchers can mitigate such stalls, but accurate prediction alone does not guarantee performance improvement: a predicted prefetch becomes beneficial only if it is worth issuing, arrives at the right time, and is retained without harmful interference. Because these requirements interact, optimizing any single dimension in isolation can simply move the bottleneck to another. We capture these requirements with a predicted-prefetch-to-realized-benefit perspective and propose SnakeCharmer, a unified backend prefetch-control framework for address-prediction-based GPU prefetchers. SnakeCharmer separates address prediction from prefetch realization: the frontend predictor generates prefetch candidates, while the backend control path jointly controls utility, timeliness, and placement by determining whether each candidate should be issued, when it should be issued, and where the returned data should be retained. SnakeCharmer realizes this control path with zero-value-aware filtering for utility, hierarchical feedback-driven distance tuning for timeliness, and a register-assisted prefetch buffer for placement. We design and implement SnakeCharmer primarily on top of Snake, and adapt the same backend-control principles to APOGEE to demonstrate that SnakeCharmer's benefits are not limited to a single frontend predictor. On an A100 GPU model, SnakeCharmer improves performance/energy efficiency by 12.8%/20.8% over Snake and by 1.7%/3.2% over APOGEE, with modest hardware overhead.

papers.title: HAWK: Heterogeneity-Aware KV Cache Transfer for Efficient GPU-NPU Phase-Disaggregated LLM Inference
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) inference exhibits distinct computational characteristics across its two phases: prefill is compute-intensive, whereas decode is more memory-bound. As a result, AI accelerators achieve varying levels of efficiency across the two phases. GPUs are well suited to prefill, but are often underutilized during decode. By contrast, NPUs can utilize their compute resources more effectively during decode. Motivated by this observation, we explore a heterogeneous architecture that integrates GPUs and NPUs, mapping prefill to GPUs and decode to NPUs to achieve high performance and efficiency. However, realizing such heterogeneous integration is challenging because LLM phase disaggregation requires KV cache transfer from prefill to decode (that is, from GPUs to NPUs), which is complicated by differences in inter-device communication mechanisms and KV cache tensor layouts. To address this, we propose HAWK, a transfer mechanism that enables rapid KV cache transfer across heterogeneous devices. HAWK establishes a remote direct memory access (RDMA) path for direct cross-device transfers while handling inter-device tensor layout discrepancies as part of the transfer process. In particular, HAWK allocates tensor-layout-aware RDMA buffers on the NPU side to match the target tensor layout. Leveraging these buffers, HAWK orchestrates data transfer from a conventional contiguous GPU RDMA buffer to the corresponding NPU buffers, allowing transferred tensors to be consumed directly without additional data rearrangement while maintaining transfer efficiency. We implement and evaluate HAWK on a system built with commercially available GPUs and NPUs, demonstrating performance within 7.88% of a GPU-only system under the same SLO constraints while achieving up to 1.26$\times$ higher power efficiency and 1.72$\times$ higher cost efficiency.

papers.title: RPolyPlan: A Unified Global Floorplanning and Legalization Framework for Rectilinear Soft Modules
papers.abstract: Floorplanning with rectilinear soft modules improves area utilization and wirelength by allowing modules to adapt to rectilinear polygon (RPoly) shapes. Existing methods typically construct rectilinear polygons through incremental refinement after obtaining a rectangular global solution, which confines polygon exploration to the neighborhood induced by the initial floorplan. This paper presents RPolyPlan, a unified framework for outline-free and fixed-outline floorplanning that directly incorporates continuously deformable rectilinear polygons into global floorplanning. To enable direct polygon optimization, we introduce a structured continuous representation and a differentiable polygon shaping model that dynamically optimizes rectilinear module shapes based on overlaps, making continuous shape optimization feasible for gradient-based global floorplanning. An augmented Lagrangian formulation robustly handles the coupled inequality constraints, provides theoretical convergence guarantees, and reduces dependence on manual penalty-parameter tuning. During legalization, minimum-cost flow and rectangular decomposition determine the target areas of subrectangles, and horizontal and vertical constraint graphs encode their geometric relations. The resulting convex legalization formulation satisfies the area, shape, separation, connectivity, and outline constraints while minimizing either the chip area or the displacement from the global floorplanning solution. Experiments on the GSRC, MCNC, and ICCAD 2023 contest benchmarks demonstrate that RPolyPlan reduces HPWL over the evaluated state-of-the-art methods by 7% and 6% in fixed-outline and outline-free experiments, respectively.

papers.title: Reorienting the Vector Axis: Restructuring FlashAttention for Long-Vector Processors
papers.abstract: A Transformer is built around attention, whose cost grows with the square of the sequence length and dominates the layer on long sequences. FlashAttention made that cost manageable by tiling the attention matrix and updating the softmax as it goes, but almost all work since has targeted GPUs. On long-vector processors one vector register can hold up to 512 single-precision numbers. The savings of a vector instruction are proportional to how much of the register it uses, so the choice of which loop to vectorize is a first-order decision. We port PyTorch's CPU FlashAttention kernel to a RISC-V CPU with 2KB vector registers and find that it reaches 16.2% of peak floating-point throughput. The kernel walks each tile one query row at a time: the product against V is vectorized along the 64-element head dimension, the softmax's per-row maximum and sum are reductions that collapse a full register to a scalar, and the software exponential's polynomial coefficients compete with tile data for vector registers and cause spilling. We propose two techniques. The first transposes the score tile and the running output so that queries lie along the contiguous axis. The algorithm and its values are unchanged. A single parameter, the number of queries in a tile, now sets the vector length of every part of the kernel and can be matched to the machine. Both reductions also disappear. The second moves the polynomial's coefficients into scalar registers, removing the spills and cutting the softmax's vector memory instructions by 78.7%. On silicon the two together cut whole-kernel cycles by 1.84 to 2.08x at a head dimension of 64, raising floating-point utilization from 16.2% to 29.7% of peak. An FPGA of the same design ranks the changes identically and scores them higher, at 2.71x.

papers.title: FIGFLEX: A Mixed-Precision FP-INT GEMM Accelerator Co-Designed with Low-Bit LLM Quantization
papers.abstract: Weight-only quantization keeps LLM activations in floating point and stores weights as low-bit integers, turning the dominant workload into floating-point-integer (FP-INT) general matrix multiplication. Recent quantizers reach a 2-3-bit average with mixed precision, but hardware has not kept pace: GPUs dequantize weights to FP16 before the tensor-core multiply-accumulate, and bit-parallel FP-INT accelerators run at a single weight precision, so fewer bits save memory but not computation. In this paper, we present FIGFLEX, an algorithm-hardware co-designed mixed-precision accelerator whose bit-parallel datapath scales throughput as precision falls. FIGFLEX contributes (1) a shift-add, radix-4 reformulation of FP-INT multiplication that fuses the multiply-accumulate into a unified, precision-flexible partial-product reduction and roughly halves the partial products, together with a novel INT3 optimization that reclaims the idle datapath radix-4 leaves at that precision; and (2) a mixed-precision quantizer that assigns each channel group its bit-width according to the error GPTQ cannot compensate, with a per-input-channel column scaling whose power-of-two normalization keeps the scaled activations out of the FP16 subnormal range, so that the quantized model maps directly onto FIGFLEX's datapath with the same accuracy as on a GPU. On LLaMA-2-7B, FIGFLEX attains 5.85 and 8.77 WikiText-2 perplexity at 3- and 2-bit average precision, lower than GPTQ, AWQ, SliM-LLM, AMQ, and QuIP# (without fine-tuning), while delivering 1.56x and 1.42x higher whole-chip throughput per area on the linear GEMMs of a 3-bit mixed-precision model than AxCore and FIGLUT, respectively.

papers.title: TernScope: Model-Hardware Co-Design for Efficient Ternary Endoscopic Segmentation
papers.abstract: Edge medical segmentation must reconcile small model size, high accuracy, and fast inference. TernScope addresses this tradeoff through model--hardware co-design, learning a compact segmentation network whose low-bit operators also simplify hardware execution. Split-channel large-kernel blocks preserve spatial context with limited computation, while branch fusion removes redundant inference paths. Ternary Progressive Quantization-aware Training (TPQ) then adapts the fused network from deep to shallow layers, through the decoder, and finally to the input and prediction layers. All 25 convolutions use ternary weights and 8-bit activations, enabling packed storage and multiplier-free computation. The resulting model uses 0.2483 M parameters and 0.0949 GMACs while retaining competitive segmentation accuracy on in-domain and external datasets. Under the same 45 nm technology, TernScope reduces compute-array area by 88.46% compared with the original Gemmini, a systolic-array accelerator with 8-bit $\times$ 8-bit multipliers. These results demonstrate a path from accurate lightweight medical segmentation to compact low-bit hardware.
